newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FIFTEEN-YEAR-OLD SET TO MAKE LEAGUE DEBUT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIFTEEN-YEAR-OLD SET TO MAKE LEAGUE DEBUT.

text.p: Fifteen-year-old Matthew Etherington is set to become one of the youngest players ever to appear in the English League on Saturday when he turns out for Peterborough.
Manager Barry Fry had to ask Matthew's head teacher for permission to play him in the second division match at Brentford.
Fry said on Thursday: "I've always said if you're good enough, you're old enough. He honestly reminds me of a young George Best. He's got one hell of a future."
Left-winger Etherington will be 15 years and 261 days old when he plays, just 103 days' senior to the league's youngest two players.

The two youngest were Albert Geldard who was 15 years 158 days when he represented second division Bradford Park Avenue against Millwall in 1929 and Ken Roberts, who was exactly the same age when he played for Wrexham against Bradford Park Avenue in 1951.
